title: Cayley's formula for the number of spanning trees of the complete graph
statement: For every natural number $n$, the number of spanning trees of the complete graph $K_n$ on $n$ vertices is $\tau(K_n) = n^{n-2}$, where the exponent is the truncated difference (so it is $0$ when $n < 2$).
hypotheses_covered: n ranges over all natural numbers
the graph is the complete graph K_n on n vertices
